components.name: Project Card
components.description: Project thumbnail card with hover lift effect.
components.html: Project Title
components.css: .ds-card-project { display: block; background: #282a36; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #44475a; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-card-project:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: #bd93f9; } .ds-card-image { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; overflow: hidden; } .ds-card-image img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-card-project:hover .ds-card-image img { transform: scale(1.05); } .ds-card-body { padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; color: #f8f8f2; transition: color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-card-project:hover .ds-card-title { color: #bd93f9; }

narrative.overview: A portfolio that opens like a film. The screen is dark — not the soft gray of an app, but the purposeful dark of an edit suite at midnight. Light comes from the work itself: thumbnails glow, the purple accent strikes like a grade LUT, and the viewer moves through projects like reels on a timeline. The system is dark, bold, and energetic, but the energy comes from the palette and typography, not from frantic motion. Interactions are refined and restrained — subtle color shifts, intentional state changes. The boldness is in the commitment to darkness and the saturation of the accent palette, not in decorative flourishes. This is a portfolio that trusts its work to command attention.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-by-commitment: Midnight Ink background is not a default — it's the scene
Accent rarity: Electric Lavender is the single voice; appears on ≤15% of any screen
Tonal depth, no shadows: surfaces stack by lightness, not box-shadow
Refined interactions: state changes are subtle color shifts, not transforms or bounces
Genre-adaptive palette: tech work gets Ice Cyan framing, creative work gets Neon Rose

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Electric Lavender appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Its scarcity is the source of its signal power. When everything is purple, nothing is.

rules.name: The Genre Switch Rule
rules.body: Tech content uses Ice Cyan framing. Creative content uses Neon Rose. The palette is a communication system, not decoration.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only font. No pairings, no display face. Distinction comes from weight and size contrast, not from introducing a second family.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are not part of the vocabulary. Depth is read from lightness, not from cast light.

dos: Do use Electric Lavender sparingly — ≤15% of any screen. Its power comes from its rarity.
Do use tonal layering for depth: Midnight Ink → Dark Slate → Elevated Slate. No shadows.
Do assign Ice Cyan to tech content and Neon Rose to creative content. The palette is a categorization system.
Do use text-wrap: balance on h1–h3 for even line lengths.
Do keep body text at 70ch max width for readability.
Do use Inter at multiple weights for hierarchy instead of introducing a second font.
Do provide a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) alternative for every animation.
Do verify contrast against Midnight Ink for any new color introduced to the system.
donts: Don't use Muted Indigo (#6272a4) for body text smaller than 18px (bold) or below. At 16px it scores 3.6:1, below the 4.5:1 AA threshold.
Don't add box-shadows. Depth is tonal. Shadows on a dark background read as dirty.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Solid Electric Lavender or Moonstone only.
Don't use glassmorphism (blurred backgrounds, glass cards). The dark system is opaque and intentional.
Don't add numbered '01 / 02 / 03' markers above sections.
Don't use all-caps tracked kickers ('PROJETOS', 'SOBRE') above section headings.
Don't include film reel, clapperboard, or wipe-transition imagery.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right as colored accents).
Don't use cream/sand/beige anywhere. The system is dark and committed.
